faqs.q: How much does a turnkey roof cost per m²?
faqs.a: The price depends on how complex the roof structure is and which covering you choose (tiles, asphalt shingles or Gerard and Satjam metal). Every roof is different, so we prepare an exact quote free of charge from your project documents or an on-site survey.

faqs.q: How long does a turnkey roof take?
faqs.a: For a typical family house (about 120–180 m² of roof), building the new timber frame, battening and laying the covering usually takes 7 to 21 working days, depending on complexity and weather.

faqs.q: What warranty do you give on the roof?
faqs.a: We give a 10-year warranty on carpentry, roof trusses and roofing work. Materials carry the manufacturer's warranty, up to 30–50 years for tiles and Gerard and Satjam systems.

faqs.q: Which countries do you work in?
faqs.a: We build roofs in the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Germany and the Netherlands. Thanks to our experience abroad, we meet the building standards of all these countries.

faqs.q: What do you need to prepare a quote?
faqs.a: Ideally the project documents. For renovations, a few photos of the roof, rough dimensions, the location and your preferred covering are enough. We reply within 24 hours.

process.title: From the first call to a finished roof
process.lead: Four simple steps. You always know what happens and when, with no budget surprises.

steps.d: You call or fill in the form. We get back to you within 24 hours.
From your drawings or an on-site survey we calculate the materials and send an exact written quote.
We order certified materials and build the roof to the manufacturer's specifications. A family house usually takes 7–21 working days.
We walk the roof with you, clean up the site and hand over the work with a 10-year workmanship warranty.

pitched.title: Turnkey Pitched Roofs – Frame, Covering, Flashing | MSroofing
pitched.desc: A turnkey pitched roof from one company: timber frame, insulation, membrane, battens, covering and flashing. 10-year warranty, a family house in 7–21 working days.
pitched.lead: We build the whole roof, from the timber frame to the last piece of flashing. You choose the covering, we handle the rest – with one 10-year warranty on the entire build-up.
pitched.card: The complete roof, from timber frame to flashing. One company, one warranty.
pitched.heroAlt: Laying roofing on a pitched roof
pitched.introTitle: One company instead of four trades
pitched.intro: On a pitched roof, things usually go wrong where two trades meet: the carpenter hands over the frame, the roofer lays the covering, the metalworker adds the flashing – and when it leaks, it's nobody's fault. We build the whole build-up ourselves, from survey and material take-off to the final details.
pitched.layersTitle: What goes into a turnkey pitched roof
pitched.layersLead: The covering is only what you see. What lies underneath decides how long the roof lasts. These are the seven layers we build, from the structure up.

layers.d: The load-bearing timber frame, made to measure. Quality timber, precise joints and treatment against wood pests and mould.
Thermal insulation between the rafters, so the attic stays warm in winter and doesn't overheat in summer.
A vapour-permeable underlay. It lets moisture out of the structure but keeps water and dust out.
Create a ventilated gap between membrane and covering, letting moisture and heat escape.
Set to the millimetre for the chosen covering. Their accuracy is what makes a roof straight and watertight.
Clay or concrete tiles, asphalt shingles, or lightweight Gerard or Satjam metal. We choose together based on the house, pitch and budget.
Ridge, verges, valleys, chimney flashing, gutters and downpipes. This is where roofs leak most often, so we never cut corners here.

pitched.note: One 10-year warranty covers every layer. When we build the whole roof ourselves, nobody can blame the previous trade.
scope: Making and fitting the roof structure, or repairing it
Clean-up and handover with a 10-year warranty

faq.q: How long does a turnkey pitched roof take?
faq.a: For a typical family house (about 120–180 m² of roof), usually 7 to 21 working days, depending on complexity and weather.

faq.q: Can you build just part of the roof?
faq.a: Yes. We can supply just the frame, just the covering, or the whole build-up. A turnkey roof is the best value though – one warranty for everything.

faq.q: Which covering should I choose?
faq.a: Tiles last extremely long but are heavier. Gerard and Satjam metal is light and spares the structure. Shingles handle complex shapes and dormers. We'll recommend one during the survey.

faq.q: What warranty do you give?
faq.a: We give a 10-year workmanship warranty on the whole build-up. Materials carry the manufacturer's warranty, up to 30–50 years for tiles and Gerard and Satjam systems.

flat.title: Flat Roofs with Bitumen Membranes – Renovation | MSroofing
flat.desc: New and renovated flat roofs with IPA modified bitumen membranes. Vapour barrier, insulation, two-layer waterproofing and parapet flashing.
flat.lead: New and renovated flat roofs with modified bitumen membranes. Two-layer waterproofing, careful parapet details and junctions that stay watertight.
flat.card: IPA bitumen waterproofing, insulation and parapet flashing.
flat.heroAlt: Torching bitumen membranes onto a flat roof
flat.introTitle: A flat roof lives or dies by its details
flat.intro: Flat roofs usually leak at parapets, penetrations and outlets, not in the middle. That's why every renovation starts with thorough substrate preparation, and every seam, junction and corner is carefully done by hand.
flat.layersLead: A flat roof has to withstand standing water, frost and sun. These are the six layers that protect it, from the structure up.

layers.d: A concrete slab or timber deck. It must be level, clean and dry – the substrate decides the quality of everything above it.
Stops moisture from inside the building getting into the insulation and reducing its performance.
Boards laid staggered and without gaps, with tapered insulation where needed so water flows to the outlets.
The first waterproofing layer, forming a reliable base for the cap sheet.
IPA modified bitumen membrane, torch-applied. Slate granules protect it from UV.
Waterproofing turned up the parapet and capped with flashing. The riskiest spot on a flat roof, so we take the most care here.

flat.note: Two layers of bitumen membrane mean double protection. Even if the cap sheet gets damaged, water won't reach the structure straight away.
scope: Inspection and assessment of the existing roof
Vapour barrier and insulation to suit the build-up
IPA base membrane and cap sheet
Junctions with parapets, penetrations and outlets
Clean-up and handover with a 10-year warranty

faq.q: Repair a flat roof or replace it?
faq.a: It depends on the state of the substrate and insulation. If the insulation is dry, new waterproofing is often enough. If it's wet, a complete new build-up pays off. We'll assess it during a free inspection.

faq.q: Why two layers of bitumen membrane?
faq.a: A two-layer system is tougher and more reliable. The base membrane forms the first waterproofing layer, and the granulated cap sheet protects it from UV and mechanical damage.

faq.q: Do you do small flat roofs, like garages?
faq.a: Yes. We do flat roofs on garages, extensions, family houses and apartment blocks.

truss.title: Roof Trusses and Carpentry – New and Repairs | MSroofing
truss.desc: Made-to-measure roof structures, repair and strengthening of old ones, timber treatment. Carpentry for pergolas, carports and canopies.
truss.lead: The roof structure carries the whole roof. We make and fit new made-to-measure frames, or repair and strengthen your existing one.
truss.card: New roof structures, repair of old ones and timber carpentry.
truss.heroAlt: New timber roof structure and battens on a family house
truss.introTitle: A long-lasting roof starts with the frame
truss.intro: Every pitched roof rests on a stable timber structure. We work with quality timber and precise joints, learned on demanding sites in Germany and the Netherlands. On renovations we first inspect the frame thoroughly and propose what to repair, strengthen or replace.
truss.layersTitle: How we build a roof structure
truss.layersLead: A roof frame is made of members that together carry the weight of the roof, snow and wind. Keep scrolling to see how we put it together.

layers.d: Timbers anchored to the external walls. They transfer the load of the whole roof into the walls of the house.
Horizontal beams that form the attic floor and take the horizontal thrust from the rafters.
The sloping members that carry the whole roof build-up and covering. Spacing and size are chosen for the covering and snow load.
A long timber under the ridge that stiffens the rafters and keeps the whole frame in line.
Horizontal ties between opposite rafters. They stop them sagging and spreading.

truss.note: We treat the timber against pests and mould before fitting it, so it's protected even where nobody can reach later.
scope: Inspection and assessment of the existing frame
Sizing for the covering and loads
Timber treatment against pests and mould
Making and fitting the roof structure
Repair, replacement and strengthening of members

faq.q: Will my old roof structure carry a new covering?
faq.a: It depends on the condition of the timber and its sizes. We inspect the frame on site. If needed, we strengthen it or recommend lightweight metal roofing.

faq.q: How can I tell if the frame is infested?
faq.a: Typical signs are insect exit holes, crumbling wood, mould or sagging rafters. If you're unsure, we'll take a look.

faq.q: Do you build pergolas and canopies too?
faq.a: Yes, we build timber structures for pergolas, carports and canopies.

tile.title: Roof Tiling – Clay and Concrete Tiles | MSroofing
tile.desc: Clay and concrete roof tiles on new builds and historic houses. Precise battening, valleys, ridge and ventilation. 10-year workmanship warranty.
tile.lead: The classic covering with an extremely long life. We lay it with precise battening, a ventilated ridge and carefully flashed valleys.
tile.card: Clay and concrete tiles with an extremely long life. New builds and historic houses.
tile.heroAlt: Clay tiles on a hipped mansard roof
tile.introTitle: A tile lasts for decades – if it's laid right
tile.intro: Clay and concrete tiles store heat well and last a very long time. They are heavier, though, so we always check the roof structure can carry them. After that, the result depends on precise battening, ventilation and how the ridge and valleys are finished.
tile.layersLead: A tiled roof is a system where every layer has a job. These are the six layers we build under and with the tiles.

layers.d: The structure, which we check first. Tiles are heavier and the frame must carry them safely.
A vapour-permeable safety layer under the covering. Moisture out, water not in.
Create the ventilated gap through which moisture and heat escape from under the tiles.
We set the batten gauge exactly to the tile model. That's what makes a straight, watertight roof.
Clay or concrete tiles laid in bond, clipped against wind uplift in exposed areas.
Ridge closed with ridge tiles on a ventilated roll. Warm air escapes, rain and snow stay out.

tile.note: A tile is only as good as the battens under it. That's why we measure and check the battening on every course.
scope: Checking the structure and its load capacity
Flashing for valleys, chimneys and abutments
Snow guards and roof windows as needed
Clean-up and handover with a 10-year warranty

faq.q: Clay or concrete tiles?
faq.a: Clay tiles are a traditional ceramic covering with a very long life and a natural look. Concrete tiles are durable and usually more affordable. We're happy to compare both for your roof.

faq.q: Can my roof structure carry tiles?
faq.a: Tiles are heavier than metal or shingles. We always check the structure before laying them. If it can't carry them, we strengthen it or recommend a lighter covering.

faq.q: What warranty do tiles have?
faq.a: The material carries the manufacturer's warranty, up to 30–50 years for quality tiles. We give 10 years on our work.

metal.title: Gerard and Satjam Metal Roofing – Installation | MSroofing
metal.desc: Gerard and Satjam metal roofing. Lightweight roofing for renovations and new builds, resistant to wind and snow. Standing-seam flashing, 10-year warranty.
metal.lead: Lightweight, durable roofing that barely loads the structure. The ideal choice for renovating older houses and for modern new builds.
metal.card: Lightweight, durable metal roofing from premium brands. Ideal for renovations.
metal.heroAlt: Family house with new Gerard metal roofing
metal.introTitle: A modern look without loading the frame
metal.intro: Gerard and Satjam metal roofing is much lighter than tiles, so on renovations the existing structure is often enough. Special surface coatings make it long-lasting and good-looking. We install it with standing-seam chimney flashing and every metalwork detail.
metal.layersLead: Metal is light, but it needs the right base and good ventilation. These are the six layers we build under and with it.

layers.d: The structure. With metal, even an older frame is often enough because the covering is so light.
Especially important under metal. It drains condensation and protects the structure from moisture.
A ventilated gap under the metal, letting moisture and heat escape.
Batten spacing matches the module of the chosen roofing, so every screw lands exactly where it should.
Gerard or Satjam sheets fixed with sealed system screws.
Ridge, verges, standing-seam chimney flashing and eaves. The details that decide whether a roof stays dry.

metal.note: A metal roof needs good ventilation. That's why we never skip the membrane and counter battens – they prevent condensation under the metal.
scope: Checking and, if needed, repairing the structure
Breathable membrane, counter battens and battens
Clean-up and handover with a 10-year warranty

faq.q: Isn't a metal roof noisy in the rain?
faq.a: With the right build-up of membrane, counter battens and insulation, rain is barely audible in the attic. Stone-chip coated roofing dampens it even more.

faq.q: Do I need to strengthen the frame for metal?
faq.a: Usually not. Metal is very light, so on renovations the existing frame is normally enough. We always check its condition though.

faq.q: What warranty does metal roofing have?
faq.a: Gerard and Satjam materials carry a long-term manufacturer's warranty of up to 30–50 years depending on the type. We give 10 years on installation.

shingle.title: Asphalt Shingles – Installation and Renovation | MSroofing
shingle.desc: Asphalt shingles laid on full timber boarding. Ideal for complex roofs, dormers and steep pitches. New roofs and renovations, 10-year warranty.
shingle.lead: Light, flexible roofing for complex roofs, dormers and steep pitches. We lay it on full timber boarding so it's completely watertight.
shingle.card: Flexible roofing for dormers, complex shapes and steep pitches.
shingle.heroAlt: Asphalt shingles on a roof with dormers
shingle.introTitle: Shingles handle shapes where others give up
shingle.intro: Asphalt shingles are light, flexible and dampen the sound of rain well. That makes them ideal for roofs with complex shapes, dormers or steep pitches. The key to a long life is solid full boarding and properly finished details.
shingle.layersLead: Shingles need a solid, level base. These are the six layers we build from the rafters to the ridge.

layers.d: The structure we fix the full boarding to.
A solid, level base of boards or panels. Without it, shingles hold neither their shape nor a seal.
A waterproofing layer under the shingles. Insurance in case wind lifts a shingle.
Metal edging that leads water away from the boarding.
Laid in bond and nailed to the manufacturer's spec. The self-sealing strip bonds them into one surface in the warmth.
Ridge of shingle caps with ventilation, so no moisture builds up under the boarding.

shingle.note: A shingle is only as good as the boarding under it. That's why we always check it on renovations and replace damaged boards.
scope: Checking structure and boarding, replacing damaged parts
Clean-up and handover with a 10-year warranty

faq.q: What roof pitch suits shingles?
faq.a: Shingles suit mainly steep and complex roofs. The minimum pitch is set by the shingle manufacturer – we'll tell you during the survey whether they suit your roof.

faq.q: Why is full boarding needed?
faq.a: Shingles are flexible and don't carry themselves. Boarding gives them a solid, level base to nail into. Without it, the roof wouldn't be watertight.

faq.q: How long do shingles last?
faq.a: Their life depends on the quality of the shingle and the installation. Quality shingles carry a long manufacturer's warranty. We give 10 years on our work.

flashing.title: Roof Flashing, Gutters and Downpipes | MSroofing
flashing.desc: Sheet metal work in titanium zinc, copper and aluminium: chimney flashing, valleys, verges, gutters and downpipes. On its own or as part of a new roof.
flashing.lead: Chimney flashing, valleys, gutters and downpipes in titanium zinc, copper or aluminium. We finish the spots where roofs leak most so they last for decades.
flashing.card: Chimney flashing, valleys, gutters and downpipes in titanium zinc, copper and aluminium.
flashing.heroAlt: Chimney flashing during a roof renovation
flashing.introTitle: Most leaks start at the metalwork
flashing.intro: The covering itself rarely leaks. Problems start where the roof meets a chimney or wall, in a valley or at the eaves. That's why we do metalwork as a craft, with an eye for detail – as part of a new roof or on its own for an existing one.
flashing.layersLead: Every piece of metal on a roof has a job. Keep scrolling to see where each one goes.

layers.d: Metalwork joins the covering and must form one watertight surface with it.
Ridge flashing seals the highest point of the roof against rain and snow.
Protects the side edge of the roof from water and wind.
Leads water from the covering into the gutter, so it doesn't run down the boarding and facade.
An eaves gutter hung on brackets with the right fall to the downpipe.
Carries water from the gutter safely to the ground, away from the foundations.
The most common leak point. We make the flashing around the chimney by hand so it fits exactly.

flashing.note: We also do metalwork on its own. A leak around the chimney or need new gutters? You don't have to replace the whole roof.

faq.q: It leaks around my chimney. Do I need a new roof?
faq.a: Usually not. Often new chimney flashing and a repair of the adjoining covering is enough. During the inspection we find exactly where the water gets in.

faq.q: Titanium zinc, copper or aluminium?
faq.a: Titanium zinc is durable and develops a natural patina over time. Copper is very long-lasting and prestigious. Aluminium is light and more affordable. We'll advise based on your house and budget.

faq.q: Do you replace just gutters and downpipes?
faq.a: Yes, we supply and fit gutters, outlets and downpipes on their own for existing roofs.
